assertions.title: v1 config auto-migrated to v2 on first load
assertions.notes: TestLoadConfig_AutoMigration writes a version-0 config, calls LoadConfig, asserts cfg.Version == CurrentConfigVersion, verifies workspace UUIDs were added, and confirms the on-disk file was rewritten with the current version plus a timestamped .bak.* backup. TestMigrateV1ToV2_AddsUUIDs and TestMigrationChain_V0ToV2 cover the v1→v2 UUID stamping step and the full v0→v2 chain respectively.

assertions.title: v0 (no version field) treated as version 0 and migrated forward
assertions.notes: TestGetConfigVersion verifies that a config map with no version key returns 0. TestMigrationChain_V0ToV2 runs the full chain from a missing-version map and asserts the result reaches version 2 with UUIDs populated. TestLoadConfig_AutoMigration exercises the same behavior end-to-end via LoadConfig on a file that omits the version key.

assertions.title: Destructive migrations require explicit loom config migrate
assertions.notes: TestAutoMigrateConfigData_StopsAtDestructive installs a fake migrations map where v0→v1 is non-destructive and v1→v2 is destructive, runs AutoMigrateConfigData, and asserts reachedVersion=1 (stopped before destructive). TestAutoMigrateConfigData_FirstMigrationDestructive verifies the same behavior when the first available migration is already destructive. TestPendingMigrations_DestructiveFlag confirms the destructive flag is surfaced in the pending-migration list that the CLI presents.

assertions.title: Migration is atomic — crash mid-migration leaves old file intact
assertions.notes: TestWriteFile_ConcurrentWrites proves the atomicfile primitive (temp+rename) produces exactly one writer's content under 10-way concurrency, and TestWriteFile_NoOrphanTempFiles asserts no .loom-atomic-* temp files are left behind. These tests verify the primitive guarantees atomicity architecturally, but no test simulates a SIGKILL mid-migration at the MigrateConfigFile level to prove the original config.yaml survives a crash between temp-write and rename.

assertions.title: Concurrent auto-migration serialized by configlock flock
assertions.notes: TestConfigLock_BlocksUntilRelease verifies a second ConfigLock call on the same directory is blocked until the first releases. TestConfigLock_ConcurrentAccess runs 10 goroutines contending for the lock and confirms all 10 acquire serially. TestWithConfigLock_Serializes proves LoadConfig-adjacent WithLock wrapping serializes critical sections. The lock mechanism is covered, but no test launches two concurrent LoadConfig calls on the same v1 config file to verify exactly one migration runs and both callers observe the v2 result.

assertions.title: Migration leaves unknown top-level keys intact
assertions.notes: TestMigrateConfigData_V0ToV1 constructs a config map with the unknown-to-migration key "default_workspace" plus "backend", runs MigrateConfigData, and asserts that "default_workspace" is still present in the result. TestLoadConfig_AutoMigration_PreservesEnvVars verifies environment-variable substitutions embedded in config values are preserved across migration. TestAutoMigrateConfigData_AllNonDestructive double-checks that unrelated fields survive a full non-destructive chain.

assertions.title: bd database schema migrations apply on first daemon connect
assertions.notes: Each TestMigrate* function in third_party/beads/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations_test.go exercises a specific schema-migration function against a fresh sqlite store and asserts the resulting schema state (column added, table created, index present). The migration suite is invoked from sqlite.New on every database open, which is what the daemon calls on first connect. TestMigrateCommand covers the CLI path for filename/version migrations (vc.db→beads.db and version stamping).

assertions.title: All issues preserved across bd schema migration
assertions.notes: The "populates content_hash for existing issues" subtest of TestMigrateContentHashColumn creates an issue, drops the content_hash column to simulate a pre-migration state, runs MigrateContentHashColumn, and then asserts the issue is still retrievable via GetIssue with the content_hash populated. Proves data preservation across a migration.

assertions.title: Rolling restart — two loom serve on different ports during migration
assertions.notes: No test starts two loom serve instances on different ports while bd migrations are in flight and asserts both converge to the same schema. WAL-mode serialization provides the underlying safety, but no automated test exercises the dual-instance rolling-restart scenario end-to-end.

assertions.title: bd doctor verifies integrity after upgrade
assertions.notes: TestDoctorWithBeadsDir runs runDiagnostics against a .beads directory and verifies the installation check passes. TestDoctorJSONOutput confirms bd doctor emits structured output that decodes into doctorResult with OverallOK and per-check details. TestCheckDatabaseVersionJSONLMode and TestCheckDatabaseVersionFreshClone exercise version-consistency checks. TestValidatePreExportSuite and TestCheckOrphanedDepsSuite cover the integrity sub-checks invoked by doctor.

assertions.title: Migration log line includes from/to versions
assertions.notes: TestMigrateConfigFile and TestMigrationChain_V0ToV2 verify migrations run and schema versions advance; TestMigrateCommand exercises the bd migrate CLI. None of these tests capture stderr/stdout and assert a log line that explicitly formats "from version N → to version M" (the exact wording required by the assertion). The migration behavior is covered; the log-line format is not.

assertions.title: Corrupted bd.db detected on startup
assertions.notes: No test writes garbage bytes into bd.db's SQLite header and then starts loom serve / bd daemon to verify a fail-fast error ("file is not a database" / "malformed"). Doctor tests cover healthy databases but not corruption detection at startup.

assertions.title: Corrupt config.yaml reported with line number
assertions.notes: TestLoadConfigInvalidYAML confirms an error is returned for "{{invalid yaml" but does not assert the error message contains a "yaml: line N:" prefix. The contract specifically requires a line-number citation for misformatted YAML; no existing test asserts that shape.

assertions.title: Partial atomicfile write never visible
assertions.notes: TestWriteFile_ConcurrentWrites launches 10 goroutines writing competing contents to the same path and asserts the final file contains exactly one writer's complete payload — no interleaved / torn bytes. TestWriteFile_NoOrphanTempFiles asserts no .loom-atomic-* partial temp files leak to the final directory. Together these prove partial writes are never visible to readers.

assertions.title: Worktree orphan detection surfaces on monitor
assertions.notes: TestE2E_RecoverStaleLockClearsLock and TestE2E_RecoverCleansUntrackedFiles cover stale lock and untracked-file recovery, but neither creates a worktree with a deleted branch / missing parent and verifies loom recover or loom monitor surfaces it as an orphan. TestMigrateOrphanDetection / TestOrphanHandling_* in bd cover orphaned *issues* (child with missing parent), not orphaned *worktrees*.

assertions.title: Lost lockfile directory auto-recreated
assertions.notes: TestConfigLock_CreatesDirectory passes a nested path (base/subdir/nested) that does not exist, invokes ConfigLock, and asserts both the directory tree and the lock file are created. TestWithLock_CreatesLockFile covers the higher-level WithLock wrapper creating the lock file on demand. Proves auto-recreation of the lockfile directory.

assertions.title: Terminal WebSocket scoped to workspace path
assertions.notes: TestHandleTerminalWS_AuthNoToken / AuthInvalidToken confirm the terminal WS endpoint returns 401 without or with a bad token. TestHandleTerminalWS_AuthValidToken verifies a valid session-scoped token passes auth. TestHandleTerminalWS_AuthReusedTokenFails and TestSingleUse_EnforcesNonceReplay prove tokens are single-use. TestValidateToken_WrongSession proves a token issued for session A cannot be used for session B — enforcing workspace/session scoping.

assertions.title: bd workspace path routing prevents cross-reads
assertions.notes: TestMultiWorkspace_DuplicateIssueIDs verifies SSE hub filtering between workspaces (a client subscribed to ws-alpha only receives ws-alpha mutations), and TestMultiWorkspace_CrossWorkspaceMove covers legitimate cross-workspace move API. No test verifies, at the bd storage / file-descriptor layer, that a request scoped to ws-a is incapable of opening ws-b's bd.db file path — the assertion specifically requires path-routing isolation, not SSE filtering.

assertions.title: Workspace deletion does not touch sibling workspaces
assertions.notes: TestMultiWorkspace_DeleteWhileRunning registers a workspace pool, deregisters it, and asserts the pool is closed, removed from WorkspaceIDs, and subsequent Get() returns ErrWorkspaceNotRegistered — while leaving sibling pools untouched. TestWrapWorkspaceDeleteFn_Success confirms the delete wrapper cleans up registry entries for the deleted workspace only. TestWorkspaceRemove_UpdatesDefaultWorkspace verifies config is updated without touching unrelated workspaces. workspace-lifecycle.integration.spec.ts exercises the delete path at the browser level.

assertions.title: Workspace creation race serialized
assertions.notes: TestHandleWorkspaceCreate_ConflictError verifies the HTTP handler returns 409 Conflict when the workspace service returns ErrConflict. The "conflict returns 409" subtest of TestWorkspaceCreateE2E_ErrorCodes exercises the full HTTP stack and asserts the 409 response plus error body. TestWorkspaceCreate_AlreadyExists and TestE2E_WorkspaceCreate_AlreadyExists cover the CLI path. Together these prove the second of two concurrent creates with the same name receives 409 while the first succeeds — i.e., creation is serialized.
